Bill.BriefDescription: Prohibiting the force-feeding of certain birds.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to forcefeeding birds; adding a new chapter toTitle 69 RCW; prescribing penalties; and providing an effective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The definitions in this section applythroughout this chapter unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Bird" includes, but is not limited to, any species ofwaterfowl such as goose, duck, or the cross breed commonly known as themulard. (2) "Foie gras" means the liver of a bird that has beenspecifically fed to produce a large, fatty liver. (3) "Forcefeeding" means any process, whether implemented by handor machine, of feeding a bird that causes the bird to ingest more foodthan a typical bird of the same species would consume voluntarily.Forcefeeding methods include, but are not limited to, delivering feedthrough a tube or other devise inserted into the bird's esophagus. (4) "Person" includes, but is not limited to, individuals,partnerships, corporations, associations, and retail and restaurantestablishments.

A person may not forcefeed a bird, or hireanother person to forcefeed a bird, for the purposes of enlarging thebird's liver beyond normal size. This section does not apply if theperson forcefeeds a bird for the purpose of improving the bird'shealth.

A person may not sell or offer to sell anyfoie gras or any product containing foie gras unless the foie gras orproduct containing foie gras originated from a state or otherjurisdiction that prohibits the practice of forcefeeding birds toproduce foie gras.

Any person who violates this chapter issubject to a civil penalty of one thousand dollars per violation foreach day the violation continues. Moneys collected under this sectionshall be deposited into the state general fund.
Section 3 of this act takes effect January1, 2012.
Sections 1 through 4 of this act constitutea new chapter in Title 69 RCW.
